name: Dusun Witu
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Gudai, Darmansyah H. 1985. A Grammar of Maanyan: A Language of Central Kalimantan. PhD thesis, Australian National University; and Darmansyah 1994 / Iper, Admojo & Dahan 2000, Fonologi Bahasa Maanyan (Pusat Bahasa)
sources.note: Not a Dusun Witu source, but Ngabut et al. 1985 class the Dusun of Dusun Selatan as a subdialect of Maanyan (31% lexical difference); these Maanyan phonologies carry explicit stress statements and are the nearest proxy if the catalog ever admits closely related-variety evidence (would need to be flagged as maan1238, not dusu1267).

sources.citation: Smith, Alexander D. 2017. The Languages of Borneo: A Comprehensive Classification. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. 724 pp.
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: not located online or in the libraries checked
sources.note: Nothing for Dusun Witu: it is listed (South Barito Regency) and its lexical forms are cited throughout the Barito chapter (pp. 168-182) for sound-change evidence; the only stress remarks in the dissertation concern Merap, Segai-Modang, Bidayuh and Malayic varieties.

sources.citation: Ngabut, C. Yus; Lambertus Elbaar; Andriastuti; Yohanes Kalamper; Aneke Erland; Teras Mihing; Diana Sofian; Delna Wati; Samuel Mihing. 1985. Dialek Bahasa Daerah di Kabupaten Barito Selatan. Jakarta: Pusat Pembinaan dan Pengembangan Bahasa. xiii+460 pp. (Internet Archive copy of Badan Bahasa eprint 16032, truncated capture; page tree rebuilt locally, 472/473 pages)
sources.note: Nothing. Ch. 2.3 'Macam-macam Bunyi dalam Bahasa Daerah di Barito Selatan' (printed pp. 14-23) gives a pooled contoid/vocoid/diphthong inventory for the Barito Selatan languages with 'Bahasa Dusun' (BD, Kec. Dusun Selatan/Dusun Utara = Dusun Witu area; village 1 = Buntok) examples; sections 2.3.1-2.3.4 cover consonants, vowels, diphthongs only. No suprasegmental section; a full-text search for stress/accent tekanan/aksen/suprasegmental/prosodi over the scanned text finds only 'aksennya' (p.456) in a remark that Bawo differs little from Lawangan. The rest is Swadesh-list wordlists per village,…

sources.citation: Hudson, Alfred B. 1967. The Barito Isolects of Borneo: A Classification Based on Comparative Reconstruction and Lexicostatistics. Data Paper 68. Ithaca: Cornell Southeast Asia Program. x+112 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Dusun Witu appears as one of the East Barito wordlists (Appendix II Part I); the 'Articulatory definitions of phonetic symbols used in word lists' (p.68, read from the page scan) has vowels, consonants and special symbols but no stress mark, and the prose (sound correspondences, lexicostatistics) has no stress statement; only prosody-adjacent remark is that pre-penultimate vowels reduce to schwa in polysyllables.
